title: GTM Healthcare Intelligence
subtitle: Data provenance and query completeness
label: Self-initiated · review of my own demo
author: Kristen Martino
summary: All four selected findings have dated verification: source disclosure and quarterly ranking on October 25, combined quota and written amounts in separate October 26 follow-ups. A later October 26 check confirmed the duplicate bookings block was removed while the combined and individual values stayed intact.
provenance: All sales and practice records used here are synthetic.
scope: Public GTM demo and portfolio data disclosures.
Selected source snapshots and recorded before-fix responses.
Five targeted requests to the production query endpoints.
Expected numbers recalculated directly from fixture rows without the query engine.
limits: The requests were purpose-selected; they are not a random sample or a model-accuracy benchmark.
This review did not test every query, security controls, production scale, or source accuracy.

The original before/after strings and five check results are October 25 records at d80dd7d. October 26 checks at a1ce674 covered three quota requests at 1:55 p.m. Eastern and three written-amount requests at 3:01 p.m. Eastern. A later three-request presentation check at 3:51 p.m. Eastern followed the separate app release at 3bde922. Source disclosures, quarterly rankings and no-show controls retain their October 25 evidence; written and malformed amounts were not rechecked by the presentation follow-up.

No app code was changed or deployed for the original assessment or its first two follow-ups; those numerical and input fixes were already deployed. The later presentation check followed a separately deployed duplicate-bookings fix. This portfolio update does not deploy app code.
No user study, patient-data review, clinical validation or measured commercial outcome is claimed.
methodNote: AI tools supported implementation, testing and analysis. Numerical expectations were recomputed from the synthetic input records; this is not an independent third-party audit.

findings.title: The public-data label was broader than the shipped snapshot.
findings.risk: A reader could infer that the displayed provider counts came from a completed CMS import. This is a review risk; no user misunderstanding was measured.
findings.observation: The earlier project summary described “synthetic and public data” beside a “CMS NPPES · Medicare PUF · Census” badge. The recorded SpectrumIQ input modes were synthetic providers and embedded demographic references.
findings.before:
…using synthetic and public data.
CMS NPPES · Medicare PUF · Census
findings.after:
Synthetic demo records.
Embedded references.
Optional public-data ingestion.
findings.fix: Publish separate disclosures for generated records, bundled references and the optional local-file loader. Avoid using a source name as evidence that ingestion occurred.
findings.verification: Verified on the public case-study page. All three labels are present and agree with the recorded input modes. Publication correction 43bdf1b; no data or calculation change is claimed.
acceptance: Display the three data paths distinctly.
Name the default snapshot’s actual input modes.
Describe public-file ingestion as optional, not a completed live import.

findings.title: Combined totals and individual results are complete and shown once.
findings.risk: The original response supplied correct individual figures but omitted the requested combined result. Without a total, a reader had to reconstruct weighted attainment from the amounts.
findings.observation: The combined-quota question returned only Chen and Kim rows on October 25. The 1:55 p.m. October 26 follow-up verified the combined total and individual quota rows but recorded repeated bookings. After a separate app release, the 3:51 p.m. check confirmed each rep appeared once while the combined and individual values stayed intact.
findings.question: What is the combined quota and attainment for Sarah Chen and David Kim in Q1 2025?
findings.before:
Chen: $504,000 bookings / $450,000 quota / 112.0%
Kim: $250,000 bookings / $350,000 quota / 71.4%
No combined result.
findings.after:
Fresh production response: the same two rep rows.
No combined quota, bookings or attainment was returned.
findings.fix: The earlier numerical fix returns combined quota and weighted attainment while preserving individual results. The later display fix at 3bde922 suppresses a fully redundant bookings block only when quota results cover the same scope, displayed metrics and values. Distinct results and the underlying calculation records remain available.
findings.verification: The October 26, 3:51 p.m. production check at revision 3bde922 passed requests for combined totals, individual results, and both together. Combined bookings $754,000 / quota $800,000 still gives 94.25% attainment (94.3% displayed). Chen and Kim each display once with their correct quota rows. The earlier repeated response is preserved in the 1:55 p.m. quota evidence.
acceptance: Return one combined result with $800,000 quota and $754,000 bookings.
Calculate attainment as 754,000 ÷ 800,000 = 94.25% (94.3% at one decimal).
Preserve correct per-rep results and supported cohort restrictions.

followUp.summary: Combined-only, per-rep-only and both-together requests passed the dated quota recheck.

findings.title: A valid quarterly ranking was rejected by the scope guard.
findings.risk: A supported question could be blocked even when the supplied tool queries covered the requested year. The observed failure was a clarification, not an incorrect number.
findings.observation: A recorded production response rejected an annual quarterly ranking. PR #22 changed coverage checks to accept valid period partitions per measure.
findings.question: Who had the most denials in each quarter of 2025?
findings.before: The shared period must apply to every independent measure.
findings.after:
Q1: Brooks — 81
Q2: Singh — 74
Q3: Brooks — 65
Q4: Yamamoto — 60
findings.fix: Accept complete quarterly partitions without accepting missing periods, swapped ranges or unsupported cohort links. This repair was implemented before the current assessment.
findings.verification: One fresh production request returned all four expected winners and counts. Expected values were recalculated directly from monthly fixture rows. This is a targeted recheck, not proof of every possible phrasing or tool plan.
acceptance: Return all four requested quarters with their own winners.
Continue rejecting genuinely incomplete or unsupported scopes.

findings.title: Written and numeric revenue thresholds now match.
findings.risk: The original written amount required clarification where the equivalent numeric form succeeded. The recheck tested the complete amount and scale, including an ambiguous quantity that must stop before calculation.
findings.observation: The October 25 written-threshold request stopped for clarification. A separate October 26 recheck returned the same normalized revenue threshold, provider result and displayed answer for written and numeric forms; a malformed quantity still stopped calculation.
findings.question: Which providers had at least one point five million in revenue in 2025?
findings.before: The numeric threshold was not preserved. Please clarify the comparison; no calculation was run.
findings.after:
Written amount: clarification again.
Numeric control (≥ $1.5M): Singh — $1,592,362.
findings.fix: The existing written-number parser preserves the complete quantity and scale, and rejects malformed quantities before tool execution. Fix 65e1db5 was already deployed before the follow-up; no app code was changed or deployed for this recheck.
findings.verification: Verified October 26 at 3:01 p.m. Eastern, serving revision a1ce674. Written and numeric forms both use revenue ≥ 1,500,000 across all 12 months and return only Singh at $1,592,362. Direct monthly sums confirm the expectation. The malformed control requests clarification, with zero tool calls and no calculation.
acceptance: Interpret one point five million as 1,500,000, or clearly ask for the supported numeric form.
Match the $1.5M control when calculation proceeds.
Never silently accept only the leading “one.”

followUp.summary: Written and numeric thresholds matched; the malformed-input control stopped without a calculation.

plan.title: Retain the duplicate-output and quota checks
plan.text: Keep each rep’s bookings, quota and attainment together once, while preserving requested totals and calculation records. plan.title: Retain the provenance and period checks

hiringNarrative.title: Analytics review work sample
hiringNarrative.opening: An AI analytics answer needs to meet the request, use the right business calculation and describe its inputs accurately. These selected checks show how those requirements were evaluated in a synthetic demo, with original failures and later verification kept together.

decisions.title: Require the complete answer
paragraphs: Correct individual figures left a combined-quota question unanswered. The required result sums bookings and quotas before calculating attainment. Requests for the total, individual results and both together were checked; averaging rep percentages would misstate the result.

decisions.title: Keep claims within the evidence
paragraphs: CMS labels overstated the snapshot’s inputs: synthetic providers and embedded demographic references. Corrected wording distinguishes those inputs from optional public-file ingestion. The data and calculations stayed unchanged.

decisions.title: Preserve clarification for ambiguous input
paragraphs: “One point five million” and “$1.5M” now apply the same minimum and return Singh: $1,592,362 for 2025. Malformed “one point five point six million” still asks for clarification, avoiding a calculation from an incomplete amount.

verification: The recorded checks confirmed complete combined and individual quota results, matching written and numeric thresholds, and removal of the repeated bookings block.

clientNarrative.title: Sample AI feature assessment
clientNarrative.opening: This example shows the format of a focused feature assessment: what failed, why it mattered, the recommended change, and how its correction was checked.

decisions.title: Source claims exceeded the inputs
paragraphs: CMS labels could suggest a completed public-data import. The displayed snapshot used synthetic provider records and embedded demographic references.
decisions.recommendation: Name those inputs separately from optional public-file ingestion.

decisions.title: A combined question returned individual rows
paragraphs: Correct rep figures left the reader to reconstruct the requested total.
decisions.recommendation: Return summed bookings and quota, then calculate weighted attainment; keep individual rows when requested.

decisions.title: Equivalent amounts behaved differently
paragraphs: “One point five million” required clarification where “$1.5M” succeeded. Both now return Singh’s $1,592,362 revenue for 2025; malformed “one point five point six million” still asks for clarification.
decisions.recommendation: Apply the same $1.5 million minimum to complete written and numeric inputs; ask for clarification when the quantity is malformed.

verification: The recorded checks confirmed complete combined and individual quota results, matching written and numeric thresholds, and removal of the repeated bookings block.
